title: Condylar movement in orthognathic surgery patients with severe malocclusion - a preliminary study using real time MRI
summary:
Real-time magnetic resonance imaging (real-time MRI) is an innovative method that allows examination of anatomical structures during movement. In particular soft tissue can be analyzed in the course of movement. In this project, the movement of the temporomandibular joints of patients with severe jaw malformations is examined and compared with that of a controll. The movement is investigated by real-time MRI and axiography. The aim is to determine specific movement patterns and to investigate their relation to skeletal morphologies.
This leads to a better understanding of mandibular movement patterns and expands our knowledge on mandibular biomechanics.
